name: Learn needle felting
blurb: Stabbing wool with a barbed needle until it becomes a solid shape. Immediate, sculptural and needs almost no equipment — though it will find your fingers.
gear: A dense foam block to work on
steps: Learn the basic action: a straight vertical stab, in and out at the same angle. Levering sideways snaps needles.
Roll a loose ball of wool and felt it until firm — the more you stab, the denser and smaller it gets.
Build shapes by adding wool in layers rather than starting with the full amount.
Learn to attach parts by leaving loose fibre at the join and felting it into the body.
Switch to a finer needle for surface finishing to hide the needle marks.
Add detail with small wisps of coloured wool.
tips: These needles are extremely sharp and barbed. Everyone stabs themselves; finger guards reduce how often.
Under-felted work stays fuzzy and falls apart. Keep going until it feels firm.
proof: A recognisable felted figure that holds its shape and has a smooth surface.
